bib.title: Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought Elicits Spatial Reasoning in Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Mind's Eye of LLMs: Visualization-of-Thought Elicits Spatial Reasoning in Large Language Models". Wenshan Wu, Shaoguang Mao, Yadong Zhang, Yan Xia, Li Dong, Lei Cui, Furu Wei (Microsoft Research; ECNU). NeurIPS 2024 (arXiv:2404.03622v3, 23 Oct 2024).

COVERAGE: All 34 pages, 79,882 chars, read in full (main text, limitations, appendices A-E, tables 4-6). References skimmed for origins. Figure-only content (Figs 8-17 model transcripts) is not in the extraction, so I did not read it. Figures tool not run.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: VoT, a zero-shot prompt that asks the model to draw the state after each reasoning step, beats CoT, "no visualization" and a multimodal model on all three spatial tasks with GPT-4.
  number: Route planning completing rate 40.77 vs 37.02 (CoT), success rate 14.72 vs 9.48; next-step prediction 55.28 vs 48.61; visual tiling 63.94 vs 54.15; natural-language navigation 59.00 vs 54.00 (CoT), 35.50 (w/o Viz), GPT-4V CoT 46.59 / 49.62 / 33.36 / 5.65.
  setup: GPT-4 1106-preview, GPT-4V vision-preview, Azure OpenAI, temperature 0, top_p 1, zero-shot. Prompts: CoT "Let's think step by step."; w/o Viz "Don't use visualization. Let's think step by step."; VoT "Visualize the state after each reasoning step." GPT-4V gets the image version of the grid. The model sees 2D grids made of emoji or special characters.
  quote: "GPT-4 CoT 37.02 9.48 48.61 54.15 54.00 / GPT-4 w/o Viz 37.17 10.28 48.49 46.98 35.50 / GPT-4V CoT 33.36 5.65 46.59 49.62 / / GPT-4 V oT 40.77 14.72 55.28 63.94 59.00"
  where: Table 1, p.7. Column order is route planning completing/success, next step, visual tiling, NL navigation.
- claim: The NL-navigation gain over the "no visualization" setting is 23.5 points. The authors only claim significance against all baselines "with p < 0.05", with an exception for the CoT comparison on NL navigation.
  number: 23.5%; p < 0.16 vs CoT on NL navigation
  quote: "in the natural language navigation task, GPT-4 VoT outperforms GPT-4 w/o Viz by 23.5%." and "while p < 0.16 is observed compared with GPT-4 CoT in natural language navigation task."
  setup: 200 generated 3x3 maps, two-sample z-test.
  where: Section 4.4 and Table 1, p.6-7
- claim: Text-grid GPT-4 beats GPT-4V on the image version of the same tasks. The authors say a grid-grounded LLM can outperform an MLLM here.
  number: GPT-4 CoT vs GPT-4V CoT, see Table 1 (e.g. tiling 54.15 vs 49.62).
  quote: "the noticeable performance gap between GPT-4 CoT and GPT-4V CoT indicates that LLM grounded with 2D grid could possibly outperform a MLLM in challenging spatial reasoning tasks."
  where: p.6
- claim: GPT-4 already visualizes sometimes under plain CoT, and VoT makes it much more reliable. The tracking rate is sensitive to the prompt wording.
  number: Complete tracking rates (VoT / CoT / w/o Viz). The extraction scrambles the Fig 5 bars, so values are unassigned: 96.2, 92.9, 87.1, 20, 1.2, 59.3, 57.4, 0.5, 18.1. Partial tracking: 99.2, 95.3, 87.4, 80.5, 1.8, 91, 59.2, 30.5, 5.5, 18.3. The legend and axis are unclear, so do not map them to settings without the figure.
  quote: "explicitly prompting LLMs to visualize their reasoning traces with VoT markedly improves the visual tracking rate, thereby enhancing overall performance." Also: "after removing "reasoning" from the prompt of VoT, the visualizations are sampled after GPT-4 generates the wrong answer."
  where: Fig 5 and Section 5.1, p.7
- claim: The visualizations are often wrong, yet the model usually decides correctly when its picture is right.
  number: Visual navigation: compliance 51.14, state accuracy 26.48, decision accuracy given an accurate picture 65.16. Visual tiling: 52.01, 24.25, 77.20.
  quote: "Visual Navigation 51.14 26.48 65.16 / Visual Tilling 52.01 24.25 77.20" and "the relatively low accuracy of state visualization (around 24%-26%) indicates a need for significant improvements"
  setup: Final visualization extracted from GPT-4 VoT outputs.
  where: Table 2, p.8
- claim: VoT can hurt where the task reduces to arithmetic without picturing.
  number: 52.5% (CoT) vs 49.5% (VoT)
  quote: "GPT-4 CoT outperforms GPT-4 VoT with 52.5% VS 49.5% among 200 test instances with ring size of 12."
  setup: Ring NL navigation, GPT-4 turns it into (15 - 3) % 12 style modular arithmetic.
  where: Section 5.2, p.8
- claim: VoT helps larger models, not small ones. LLAMA3-70B gains on route planning, success rate and NL navigation, with no gain on tiling. GPT-3.5 and LLAMA3-8B show mixed or no gain.
  number: LLAMA3-70B CoT to VoT: route completing 19.90 to 30.24, success 2.62 to 5.85, next step 49.01 to 54.09, tiling 56.41 to 56.03, NL nav 26.00 to 32.50. GPT-3.5: 16.10 to 19.02 route, but next step 17.42 to 13.10 and success 2.62 to 1.61. LLAMA3-8B: 4.65 to 4.97, next step 28.73 to 26.75.
  quote: "LLAMA3-70B CoT 19.90 2.62 49.01 56.41 26.00 / LLAMA3-70B V oT 30.24 5.85 54.09 56.03 32.50"
  setup: Same tasks, greedy decoding. GPT-3.5 via Azure, version string "1106-preview" as printed.
  where: Table 3, p.9
- claim: The benefit is larger for bigger models and holds at higher difficulty in next-step prediction.
  number: GPT-4 at k=7 (1488 maps): CoT 45.30, VoT 52.69. At k=5: 50.78 vs 64.06. At k=3: 68.75 vs 62.50 (VoT worse). LLAMA3-70B k=7: 46.71 vs 52.35.
  quote: "VoT method generally maintains a higher accuracy compared to CoT"
  where: Table 6, p.20
- claim: Small models fall back on random guessing, and accuracy is erratic across difficulty levels.
  number: none
  quote: "in the route planning task, GPT-3.5 CoT often resorts to speculative responses, random guessing in nearly half of the instances, which leads to exhaustion of output tokens."
  where: Section 5.3, p.9
- claim: Telling the model "use ascii-art" raises tracking and accuracy a little. The authors guess that ascii-art in code comments from pre-training is why this works. This is a conjecture, not tested.
  number: Complete tracking 98.5% (+78.5%); NL navigation accuracy 62.5% (+3.5%).
  quote: "when GPT-4 is prompted with "use ascii-art to visualize", the complete tracking rate increases to 98.5% (+78.5%), boosting task performance to 62.5% (+3.5%)."
  where: Appendix C, p.19
- claim: Model behaviour in traces. About 30 different symbols are used to track state. Language and picture often disagree. Sometimes the model spots its own bad picture and corrects itself.
  number: "Nearly 30 different symbols"
  quote: "Nearly 30 different symbols found in the navigation tasks to track the navigation progress"
  where: Appendix E, p.20-21

DATASETS / SETUP
- NL navigation: 200 3x3 maps, 9 landmarks in snake-order traversal.
- Visual navigation: 496 maps, 2520 next-step QA instances; k=2..7 roads (route planning 8/16/32/64/128/248 maps), maps up to 7x9 / 9x7.
- Visual tiling: 5x4 rectangle, 5 pieces (2 I, 2 T, 1 L tetromino), 2 or 3 masked pieces, 796 QA instances (376 configurations).
- Route planning scoring: sequences over 100 instructions are rejected as guesses. Completing rate is the mean of t/k. Success is t == k.
- Next-step and tiling are multiple choice. NL navigation is scored by sub-string match.
- Everything is zero-shot. There is no few-shot comparison.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: "This work only scratches the surface"; VoT depends on emergent ability in advanced LLMs, so smaller models and harder tasks may degrade; tracking is prompt-sensitive; images tested are only 2D grids (3D is shown only as an appendix example, Fig 11).
- Absolute performance is low. Route planning success rate is 14.72% even with VoT, and the authors say it is "far from perfect".
- Only GPT-4 1106-preview, GPT-4V, GPT-3.5, LLAMA3-8B and 70B were tested. No frontier reasoning models (this has dated; models since 2024 may behave differently). Greedy decoding, single run, no variance reported beyond z-tests.
- GPT-4 vs GPT-4V compares text grid vs emoji image. It is not a clean test of MLLMs in general.
- The cognitive "mind's eye" framing is an analogy. The paper does not probe internals.
- VoT gains are modest on several settings (about 3-4 points on route planning). Some are not significant (NL nav vs CoT p<0.16). Small models show no gain or a drop.
- No cost or token-count comparison is reported.

BUILDS ON: Chain-of-thought / zero-shot CoT (Kojima et al. 2023, "Let's think step by step"); visuospatial sketchpad (Baddeley 1992); mental images (Shepard 1978), mental rotation, Tolman 1948 cognitive maps; natural-language navigation task (Yamada et al. 2023); Mind's Eye simulation (Liu et al. 2022); LLM as world model (Hao et al. 2023); polyomino tiling (Golomb 1966) with SAT solvers and dancing links (Knuth 2000); ascii-art in code (Regehr 2019).

CODE: none. The only code-like item is the prompt itself (VoT: "Visualize the state after each reasoning step."; Section 3, p.4 and Section 4.1, p.5-6). Task template example (Fig 6/7): "Starting from [home], provide the steps to navigate to [office]." followed by "Visualize the state after each reasoning step."

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): contrasts conventional prompting, CoT and VoT, where thought and visualization alternate.
- Fig 4 (p.5): VoT outputs on the three tasks, showing the interleaved text and grid state.
- Fig 5 (p.7): tracking rates by setting. Its numbers are scrambled in the extraction.
- Fig 10 (p.22): the symbol styles the model uses to track state (arrows, pins, numbers, removed roads).
- Fig 8 (appendix): CoT vs VoT output, and the effect of removing "reasoning" from the prompt.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The Fig 5 bar values are interleaved and unassignable. Table 1 column headers wrap awkwardly, so I inferred the order from the header text; GPT-4V has "/" for NL navigation (no image counterpart). "V oT" is a spacing artifact for "VoT". In Table 3 the GPT-3.5 model version is printed "1106-preview" (as in the paper). Appendix figure transcripts (Figs 11-17) were not readable as text.
